declared.title: Wealth redistribution promotes happiness.
declared.venue: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
declared.foundIn: Europe PMC search « (lottery OR windfall OR "cash transfer") AND (happiness OR "life satisfaction" OR "well-being") AND (replication OR preregistered OR "meta-analysis") » (2026-11-22)

population: adults in Brazil, Indonesia, Kenya, US, UK, Canada, Australia recruited online; 200 randomly given $10,000, 100 controls

findings.text: Receiving $10,000 raised well-being over the next 3 months compared with controls who received nothing

support.sentence: Our preregistered analyses offer causal evidence that cash transfers substantially increase happiness among economically diverse individuals around the world.

findings.text: The same gift brings about three times more well-being in lower-income countries than in higher-income ones

support.sentence: Recipients in lower-income countries exhibited happiness gains three times larger than those in higher-income countries.

findings.text: The gift still raised well-being for households earning up to $123,000 a year

support.sentence: Still, the cash provided detectable benefits for people with household incomes up to $123,000.

limits: small sample (300) recruited through Twitter, well educated: not representative
well-being measured over 3 months (preregistered) and at 6 months (exploratory): says nothing about years
« happiness » is an index of life satisfaction, positive and negative feelings combined
« three times larger » (by country) and « up to $123,000 » come from exploratory analyses, not preregistered ones (full text)
in higher-income countries the gain is at the edge of significance (p = 0.05), as is the benefit at $123,000 (full text)
